en: The Auspicious Morning Prayer to Śrī Kāmākṣī.
O Mother Goddess Kāmākṣī, just as the poet Mūka became mute by your glance from the mountain,
so do you act, O Consort of the Supreme Lord.
Bowing at the base of your feet, [I am] moistened with compassion.
Arise, arise, O Giver of Boons; arise, O Sovereign of the World!
Arise, O Support of the Universe, and bestow auspiciousness upon the three worlds. ||1||
Do you hear this sound arising from the mṛdaṅgas, bherīs, paṭahas, and ānakas,
as well as the Vedic chanting of the learned Brahmins?
Do you hear, O blessed lady? May there be a beautiful dawn.
Do you not hear, O blessed lady, the sound of conchs and the sweet singing of the bards? Do you not hear, O mother, the calls of the cuckoos and the cocks?
Make a sound at dawn; may there be a beautiful dawn.
O Mother, beholding your face, the Lord Moon, overcome with shame, has entered his own abode;
and the Lord Sun likewise enters his dwelling to behold your countenance.
O Goddess, he is coming to your abode; perform the auspicious morning rite. ||4||
"Behold, Mother! Some carry jars filled with ghee;
some, out of compassion, wear garlands of flowers;
and some, with beautiful limbs, hold musical instruments in their hands."
They remain; O Kuru, may there be a beautiful dawn for them. ||5||
O Goddess, beloved of Maheśa, the chanters of praise stand with drums, mṛdaṅgas, paṇavas, and ānakas in their hands, desiring your moment to offer hymns to you.
Arise now from your divine couch; make this dawn auspicious.
O Mother, behold your own face; the Blessed One has not risen, thinking it to be the moon, but remains lying upon your lap.
O Girijā, awaken him quickly; it is a pure dawn.
O beloved of Maheśa, grant a beautiful dawn to all that has been born. ||7||
Hearing the jingling sound of your anklets and bracelets as you move within,
I am eager for a sight of you at dawn.
I stand at the door; grant me a fair morning. ||8||
Sarasvatī is the book, Ambikā is the daughter of the mountain, Padmāsanā is the lotuses, Rambhā is the splendor of the sky, Girijā is the Gaṅgā, and the Gaṅgā is the water;
Kālī is the pair of cymbals, Bṛndā is the pair of mṛdaṅga drums, and likewise Nandā.
Holding a stainless blue mirror, she [graced] their auspicious morning. ||9||
Having risen from his bed, O Goddess Girijā, the Blessed Lord, the Foe of Tripura, proceeds to bathe in the celestial river;
for the Compassionate One does not delight in going alone, O Sinless One.
Arise now, O Goddess, from your bed; grant us a beautiful morning.
See, O Mother, some with fruits and flowers in their hands; others, O Mother, recite the Purāṇas;
and many recite the Vedas on your day.
Grant a fair dawn to those people. ||11||
Having long gazed upon the treasure-trove of your loveliness, even the destroyer of Kama’s pride has fallen under your sway;
for your pair of cheeks have been kissed by the enemy of Kama.
We stand here now to see you; O Kuru, may your dawn be auspicious! ||12||
O Gaṅgā, many lords of sages, having brought water from the Ganges,
carry jars upon their heads and long for you in order to bathe you with the waters of the Ganges.
O Bestower of Boons, standing at the door, grant us a beautiful dawn. ||13||
O Mother, garlands fashioned by the florist from mandāra and kunda flowers, as well as from jasmine blossoms—
these enchanting wreaths are offered even at Your divine feet.
The sages remain here, O Queen; grant them a fair morning.
Her rounded hips are embraced by a girdle of bells,
the region of her throat is anointed with saffron sandalwood paste,
her cheeks are kissed by Kāmeśa, and her nose is noble.
We stand here now to behold you; O Kuru, may there be a glorious dawn for you! ||15||
O deer-eyed one, [behold] His gentle smile, His pure, beautiful, and wide eyes, His neck as fair as the tender interior of a lotus,
and the pair of His feet marked with the wheel.
We stand here desiring to see you; now, O Kuru, make it a beautiful dawn.
I wish to behold your gentle smile— the smile of the Enemy of Tripura that destroyed the three cities, the smile of Kāmeśvara that removes the anger born of love,
and your gentle smile that precedes a broad laugh.
O Mother, we stand here; now grant us a blessed dawn. ||17||
In this world, a mother does not succumb to the power of sleep for the sake of protecting her children;
you are the mother who is the refuge of the three worlds.
Always remaining awake, bring about a beautiful dawn. ||18||
O Mother, whose feet are worshipped by Murāri and Kamalāsana,
I desire to hear your words— heart-pleasing, divinely sweet, captivating, and bestowers of auspiciousness.
We stand at the door; O Mother, grant us a beautiful dawn. 19.
Though he was naked, holding a skull of Brahmā in his hand,
with disheveled hair and his body entwined by serpents,
nevertheless, O Mother, through union with you, O Goddess—
He became Maheśvara; may there be a beautiful dawn for you. ||20||
O Goddess, it was indeed by drinking the milk you gave that the Dravidian child became the very embodiment of the union with knowledge;
Bhavānī [drank] the remainder of the milk once enjoyed by the son of the Dravidian.
O Mother, if you grant me this, my morning shall be truly auspicious.
O Mother, O Goddess Bhavānī, although he was but an infant, your son, by the power of drinking your breast milk,
awakened the specific meaning of the syllable Om (praṇava) at the root of your husband's ear.
If you have compassion for me, may it be a beautiful dawn for me.
Are you the large-eyed consort of Viśvanātha? Or perhaps the fish-eyed consort of Hālāsyanātha? Or are you the desire-eyed consort of Ekāmranātha?
O wife of Kāmeśa, grant a beautiful dawn! ||23||
O venerable Śrī Candraśekhara, my refuge!
Filled with devotion for your feet and holding fruits and flowers in my hands,
I am a seeker of your vision, O beloved of Ekāmranātha.
This best of ascetics remains; for me, it is a truly auspicious dawn. ||24||
O beloved of Ekāmranātha, you are indeed worshipped in Kāmapīṭha by the boon-granting Guru Śaṅkara;
O Goddess whose feet are honored by the most excellent of gurus, beginning with Śrī Śaṅkara!
We have come here to see you; O Kuru, grant us a fair morning.

O Mother, I stand here to behold those two who are skilled in pacifying misfortune, capable of destroying death and its progeny, the bestowers of liberation and wisdom upon those who have approached their feet, with hands granting fearlessness and boons.
O noble lady, wife of the destroyer of Tripura, may there be a beautiful dawn for me! 26.
O Mother, [I wish] to behold that foot of His— which is marked with the signs of the discus, the lotus, and the conch, which is worthy of being worshipped by Viṣṇu,
Brahmā, and the others, and which is the royal swan for the minds of yogis.
I stand at the door, O Giver of Boons; grant me a beautiful dawn.
Let some behold your face; let others praise your auspicious qualities;
and let your own devotees bow at the pair of your lotus feet.
Grant a beautiful dawn to those standing at the gate. ||28||
Some may see him on the exceedingly lofty peak of Mount Sumeru;
some on the vast and excellent Maṇidvīpa; and others within the ocean of nectar.
I see you here; it is a beautiful dawn.
Seated upon the left lap of Śambhu, with a face like the moon, eyes as broad as blue lotuses,
dark-limbed, with a beautiful smile, possessing very full breasts and lips like the ripe bimba fruit—
Kāmākṣī, the bestower of desires, her mass of hair curled, her limbs adorned with ornaments.
Let us behold [the Lord] at the beautiful dawn; today, for us whose lives are bowed in devotion, let there be a truly auspicious morning.
O wish-fulfilling tree that grants all desires, you shine forth; indeed, I have no other resort, for I am like a cātaka bird.
May you pour down showers of golden rain, for the rain of the clouds is never in vain.
But let some streams be directed toward me quickly. ||31||
I bow to the beloved of Trilocana; I bow to Tripurasundarī;
I bow to the Mistress of the Three Worlds. O Ambikā, may there be a beautiful dawn for me! 32.
O Mother Kāmākṣī, by your compassionate glance,
this indeed has been made a beautiful dawn for me;
O Mother, I have obtained immediate fruit in the form of happiness.
And thus indeed has my state of suffering come to pass. ||33||
Or those who at dawn recite "Excellent Dawn" with devotion before you, O Noble One,
or those whose minds are fixed upon you who listen [to it].
Bring about a beautiful dawn for them—a truly auspicious morning. ||34||
Thus ends the *Śrī Kāmākṣī Suprabhātam*.
